battle.name: 美菲戰爭
battle.theater: 呂宋中部與馬尼拉灣沿岸
battle.brief: 一八九九年二月四日，革命軍與美軍在馬尼拉近郊帕西格河畔開火，美菲戰爭開打。美軍以三吋口徑的線膛野戰砲為砲兵骨幹，革命軍則用西班牙時期留下的舊銅砲與船載砲位作戰。雙方在呂宋中部的中央區拉鋸三年，一九〇二年革命政府垮台，戰事以《華盛頓條約》收場。

kit.name: 線膛砲
kit.history: 線膛讓同樣的藥量走得更遠。砲兵第一次可以在射程上贏步兵。

countries: 交戰的兩方，是美國與宣稱獨立的菲律賓革命軍，說白了是一個剛建成的共和政府與它的前宗主國背後的新主人。美國一方由陸軍部指導，戰區指揮分兩層：全國部隊的指揮權在首都的陸軍參謀總部，駐菲最高指揮官先後由喬治·沃德·邁爾斯與亞瑟·麥克阿瑟接任，軍政總督一職先後由亞瑟·麥克阿瑟與威廉·塔夫脫接任，塔夫脫於一九〇一年改任文職總督。駐軍編制以常備步兵團為骨架，另徵召三十餘個美國義勇步兵團，其中第二十六、二十七、二十八等新編團被拿來試驗小分隊作戰與追擊戰術。步兵的標準槍械是葛拉格－約根森步槍，砲兵主力是三吋口徑線膛野戰砲，另有七磅、十五磅野戰砲與可拆件山砲；海上由亞洲艦隊的裝甲巡洋艦與運輸船隊負責封鎖沿岸與維持補給。菲律賓一方的軍隊源自一八九六年反西班牙的蓋蒂普南運動，經一八九八年馬尼拉易手後擴張為革命軍，一八九九年一月馬洛斯國會通過共和憲章、成立馬洛斯共和國，總統艾米利奧·阿吉納爾多主持；軍隊按師、旅、營編制，設砲兵營與工兵隊，地方上另有以邦鎮為基礎的武裝。此外戰線上還存在兩種中間力量：站在西班牙一方的菲籍效忠派民兵，以及美方另行扶植的地方保安隊與義警。西班牙殖民當局於一八九八年八月在馬尼拉投降，其留下的軍械庫、要塞、鐵路與財政，全部成為美軍接手的基礎，也成為革命軍與美軍爭奪的物資來源。
countriesEn: The two sides in this war were the United States on one hand and, on the other, the Philippine revolutionary army, which claimed to represent an independent state — in effect a newly created republic facing the new master of its former colonial lord. The American side was guided from Washington by the War Department, and command on the ground worked in two layers: the overall chain of command sat in the Army General Staff in the capital, the highest commander in the islands passed in turn from George W. Miles to Arthur MacArthur, and the post of military governor passed to MacArthur and then to Taft, who turned it into a civilian governorship in 1901. The garrison was built on a skeleton of regular infantry regiments, supplemented by more than thirty American volunteer infantry regiments, of which the Twenty-Sixth, Twenty-Seventh and Twenty-Eighth and similar newly raised formations were used to test small-unit operations and pursuit tactics. The standard infantry arm was the Krag-Jørgensen rifle; the backbone of the artillery was the 3-inch rifled muzzle-loading field gun, supported by seven- and fifteen-pounder field pieces and by packable mountain guns; at sea the armored cruisers and transports of the Asiatic Squadron kept the coast blockaded and the supply line alive. The Philippine army grew out of the Katipunan movement against Spain of 1896, expanded enormously when Manila changed hands in 1898, and became the revolutionary army proper once the Congress at Malolos passed the republican charter in January 1899, creating the Malolos Republic under President Emilio Aguinaldo; its forces were organised into divisions, brigades and battalions with an artillery corps and engineer units, and at village level there were armed bands organised on the barangay. Two intermediate groups also appear on the line: Filipino loyalist militia who stayed with Spain, and local constabulary and volunteer forces sponsored by the American authorities. The Spanish colonial government capitulated at Manila in August 1898, and the arsenals, forts, railways and treasury it left behind passed wholesale to the Americans, becoming both the base of the American war effort and the stock of matériel fought over by revolutionaries and Americans alike.
people: 關鍵人物分屬兩個營地，各自有一位主導者。革命方的核心是艾米利奧·阿吉納爾多：他原是「馬加洛」地方勢力的首領，一八九六年加入蓋蒂普南，一八九七年三月在特耶羅斯大會取得革命主導權；一八九八年五月比亞克納巴托條約引發革命方分裂，他一派拒絕條約、擴大攻勢，同年九月在西班牙喪失海上補給之後率軍攻入馬尼拉接管城防，年底以「中央政府」名義控制呂宋大部，一八九九年一月主持馬洛斯國會並就任馬洛斯共和國總統。他的政策由幕僚長阿波利納里奧·馬比尼實際起草，馬洛斯憲章、政府的建制方案與以卡維特至維甘為軸的國防計畫都出自我手，馬比尼在香港與新加坡一帶奔走籌款徵募，後期親赴中央區組織抵抗。革命奠基者安德烈斯·博尼法西奧於一八九二年創立蓋蒂普南，一八九六年的「普加德勞溫起義」由他發動，一八九七年三月在特耶羅斯大會上把領導權讓給阿吉納爾多，自己在同年五月一次交火中陣亡。地方一級有馬里亞諾·特里亞斯、皮奧·德爾·皮拉爾、潘塔萊昂·加西亞等一批將領；提拉德隘口由格雷戈里奧·桑西安科與福斯蒂諾·薩爾蒙指揮，以六十人不到的兵力硬守山道；巴萊爾守軍由薩圖爾尼奧·馬丁·切雷索中校率領，這支隊伍在對西班牙作戰的最後一役中撐到一八九九年十二月。美國一方，總統威廉·麥金萊決定用兵並拒絕承認革命政府的地位，國務卿約翰·海伊主持對外談判並強調用兵而不住辱當地人，陸軍部長伊萊胡·魯特在華盛頓掌握指導方針，他於一九〇〇年發出的通令要求結束戰事並反對軍方採取的殘酷手段，在外人面前指責過美軍的作風。亞洲艦隊司令格魯·杜伊曾在馬尼拉海戰中擊沉西班牙艦隊，其後由約翰·沃森接任，執行沿岸封鎖。喬治·沃德·邁爾斯是駐菲美軍的實際指揮者，在卡迪巴沼澤一線屢屢受挫；一九〇〇年四月接手的亞瑟·麥克阿瑟主張追擊到馬洛斯，其嚴厲作風在巴丹加斯與薩馬爾引發爭議，一九〇一年被召回。他正是日後那位道格拉斯·麥克阿瑟之父。
peopleEn: The decisive personalities belonged to two camps, each with its own driving figure. At the centre of the revolutionary side was Emilio Aguinaldo: originally a local leader of the Magdalo, he joined the Katipunan in 1896 and took over the leadership of the revolution at the Tejeros conference in March 1897; the Pact of Biak-na-Bato in May 1898 split the revolutionary side in two, and his faction refused the pact and widened the war; after Spain lost its sea supply in that year he marched into Manila and took over the city in September of that year, extended the authority of a central government over most of Luzon before the year ended, and in January 1899 presided over the Congress at Malolos and became president of the Malolos Republic. The actual drafting of policy fell to his chief adviser Apolinario Mabini, who wrote the Malolos charter, the plan for the structure of government and the defensive scheme built on the Cavite-Vigan line; Mabini travelled through Hong Kong and Singapore raising money and men, and later entered the central zone to organise resistance. The founder of the revolution, Andrés Bonifacio, created the Katipunan in 1892 and launched the Cry of Pugad Lawin in 1896; at the Tejeros conference in March 1897 he yielded the leadership to Aguinaldo, and he was killed in an engagement in May of the same year. At provincial level there was a generation of commanders — Mariano Trias, Pío del Pilar, Pantaleon García among them; the defense of Tirad Pass was led by Gregorio Sancianco and Faustino Salmon with fewer than sixty men holding the mountain track; and the garrison at Baler was commanded by Lieutenant Colonel Saturnino Martín Cerezo, the formation that held out in the last battle against Spain until December 1899. On the American side, President William McKinley decided on the use of force and refused to recognise the revolutionary government, while Secretary of State John Hay directed the negotiations and insisted that force be used without humiliating the population; Secretary of War Elihu Root guided policy from Washington and, in a circular of 1900, demanded that the war be ended and the conduct of the army in the field be rebuked in public. George Dewey, commanding the Asiatic Squadron, had destroyed the Spanish fleet in the battle of Manila Bay, and was succeeded by John Watson, who ran the blockade of the coast. George W. Miles was the practical commander of the American forces in the islands and was repeatedly checked in the Candaba swamps; in April 1900 Arthur MacArthur took over, pressed the pursuit to Malolos, and his severity in Batangas and Samar brought him into dispute, so that he was recalled in 1901. He was the father of the Douglas MacArthur of later fame.
kits: 卡面這件一八五〇年的德製前裝線膛野戰砲，技術上代表的是一八五〇年代普魯士砲兵完成的一次變革：加長炮膛、在膛壁刻上膛線、配合密閉火室，讓同樣藥量的長形彈丸飛得更遠，砲兵第一次能在射程上壓過步兵。這個類型到一八九九年已走完一生：德國本身早已改用後膛砲，革命軍手裡的舊砲多半是西班牙時期留下的銅件，美軍的野戰砲雖然同樣是前裝，卻已是膛線更精密、射程更遠的後一代製品。真正把這條血脈延續到這場戰役裡的，是美軍的三吋口徑線膛野戰砲：青銅質、自重約一千一百磅，發射帶可發射十二發，最大射程約五千八百公尺，是美軍在呂宋的標準野戰砲，砲組由工兵以馬匹牽引，配屬七磅與十五磅野戰砲、可拆成數件由騾子馱運的三十七毫米山砲，以及加特林與麥克辛機關砲；海上的重火力由裝甲巡洋艦的八吋主砲提供，砲擊沿岸陣地。革命軍的砲兵則相當寒酸：馬洛斯政府的編制上有砲兵營，實際投入的多是從西班牙軍械庫與馬尼拉要塞接收的舊銅砲，膛徑小、射程短；巴萊爾守軍用的是一門四點三吋迫擊砲，提拉德隘口守軍配有一門小型銅砲，其複製品現陳列於隘口的紀念館。步兵武器方面，革命軍以西班牙的毛瑟步槍、雷明登步槍與左輪手槍為主，另有一八九九年在布拉干聖米格爾被美軍發現的武器窖藏，登記數量約四萬支步槍與約二百萬發子彈，可見雙方在武器供應上遠不成比例。運輸與馭獸是另一個瓶頸：呂宋缺少可通行車馬的道路，雨季一到，美軍只能靠騾子、水牛與人力車隊運送彈藥與糧食，火砲一旦失去牽引便寸步難行，革命軍則以本地水牛、竹筏與內河小船在帕西格河與邦板牙河上轉運。
kitsEn: The muzzle-loading field gun on this card, a German piece of 1850, represents technically the transformation the Prussian artillerymen completed in the 1850s: lengthening the chamber, cutting rifling into the bore, and fitting a sealed chamber so that the same charge of powder threw a longer projectile further, and artillery won on range against infantry for the first time. By 1899 the type had lived out its life: Germany itself had long since gone over to breech-loaders, the old guns in revolutionary hands were mostly Spanish-period brass, and the American field pieces, though also muzzle-loading, belonged to a later generation with finer rifling and longer reach. What actually carried this bloodline into the campaign was the American 3-inch rifled muzzle-loading field gun: a bronze piece of about eleven hundred pounds, firing twelve rounds a minute on a belt, with a maximum range of some five thousand eight hundred metres. It was the standard field gun of the US Army in Luzon, drawn by horses under the engineer corps, and supported by seven- and fifteen-pounder field pieces, thirty-seven millimetre mountain guns broken down for mule transport, and Gatling and Maxim guns; heavy firepower at sea came from the eight-inch guns of the armored cruisers, firing against positions ashore. The revolutionary artillery was a poor thing: the Malolos government had an artillery corps on paper, but what actually went into action was largely old brass inherited from the Spanish arsenals and the Manila forts, of small calibre and short reach; the garrison at Baler had one 4.3-inch mortar, and the defenders of Tirad Pass had a small brass gun whose replica is displayed today in the pass memorial museum. As for infantry weapons, the revolutionaries relied on Spanish Mauser rifles, Remington rifles and revolvers, and on the arms cache uncovered by the Americans at San Miguel in Bulacan in 1899, whose inventory lists roughly forty thousand rifles and some two million rounds of ammunition, a measure of how completely unequal the supply of weapons on the two sides was. Transport and draught animals were the other bottleneck: Luzon had few roads passable by wagon or horse, and once the rains came the Americans could move ammunition and rations only on mules, carabao and human cart trains, a gun that lost its draught was a gun that stayed where it stood, while the revolutionaries shifted their supplies over the Pasig and the Pampanga on carabao, bamboo raft and river boat.
tactics: 美軍在呂宋的作戰分成前後三段，砲兵的用法也隨之改變。一八九九年的正面會戰階段，美軍照搬歐洲經驗，以營為單位成列推進，砲兵先用三吋線膛野戰砲建立射程優勢，再由步兵上射擊陣地；但二月馬尼拉之戰與卡拉俄坎之戰都顯示，這套打法在缺乏道路、稻田與村落作掩體的鄉間無從展開，砲兵一旦失去馬匹牽引就寸步難行，彈藥一旦斷供便全線停擺。第二段是一九〇〇年後的搜索作戰：美軍改以連、排為單位的小分隊，沿唯一可用的馬車路與小徑推進，每支分隊只攜帶二十日份口糧，砲兵多改為可拆件由騾子馱運的山砲，與後方以野戰電話線維持聯絡；這些分隊在邦板牙河與卡迪巴沼澤一帶的推進，因補給線過長而一再受挫。第三段是一九〇〇年秋之後的集中區域政策：美軍在巴丹加斯與薩馬爾出動師級部隊，系統搜索游擊隊的藏身地，把居民集中到指定地區，破壞沿途住屋、糧食與農具，切斷游擊隊與鄉村的補給關係；薩馬爾方面的指揮官惠勒將軍因此受到指責，軍部內部分裂成嚴厲與溫和兩派，陸軍部長魯特公開表示不接受軍方的作風。革命軍的戰術則自始以游擊為主：靠密集村落的群眾支持作戰，馬洛斯政府成立後成建制部隊被解散或改編，剩餘者以小隊分散到各鄉，趁夜色接近、以短程射擊襲擊小隊與哨位，再退回沼澤與山嶺；提拉德隘口守軍的做法最具代表性，在狹窄山道上以倒V字佈防，居高臨下射擊隘口的美軍縱隊，海拔約八百公尺的山口成了整條補給線的瓶頸，用延遲而非決戰換取時間。巴萊爾的六十人守軍採取壕溝加迫擊砲的據點防守，在四個多月裡以火力封鎖通往據點的正面道路。整體而言，這是一場砲兵射程優勢難以發揮、而步槍射程與補給線長度決定勝負的戰爭。
tacticsEn: The American campaign in Luzon ran in three phases, and the use of artillery changed with each of them. In the phase of pitched battle in 1899 the Americans transplanted European practice, advancing in battalion columns with the artillery first establishing a range advantage from the 3-inch field gun and the infantry then taking up firing positions; but the battles of Manila and Caloocan in February showed that this method could not be carried out in a countryside without roads, rice paddies and villages to take cover from: once the guns lost their draught they could not move, and once ammunition ran out the whole line stopped. The second phase was the small-unit war of 1900 onwards, when the Americans switched to platoons and detachments moving along the few wagon roads and paths that existed, each carrying twenty days of rations, the artillery largely reduced to mountain guns that could be broken down and carried by mule, and contact with the rear maintained by field telephone lines; the advance of these detachments through the Pampanga valley and the Candaba swamps was repeatedly checked by the length of their supply line. The third phase, from the autumn of 1900, was the policy of reconcentration: the Americans moved divisions into Batangas and Samar, systematically searched the ground where the guerrillas hid, moved the population into designated areas, and destroyed houses, food and tools along the way so as to cut the guerrillas off from the villages that fed them; the commander in Samar, General Wheeler, was censured for it, the army split into a school of severity and a school of softness, and the Secretary of War, Root, declared in public that he would not accept the conduct of the army. The revolutionaries fought as guerrillas from the start, drawing on the dense village communities; once the Malolos government was set up the formed units were disbanded or converted, and the rest dispersed into small bands that used the dark to close on isolated detachments and pickets, firing at short range and falling back into the marshes and the hills. The defense of Tirad Pass is the clearest example: a reversed V across a narrow track, firing down on the American column from above, a pass at some eight hundred metres elevation that became a bottleneck for an entire supply line, buying time by delay rather than by decision. The sixty men at Baler fought a fortified defense of trenches and mortar, using their fire to seal the single approach to the position for more than four months. Taken as a whole, this was a war in which the reach of the artillery could not be exploited and where the effective range of the rifle and the length of the supply line settled the contest.
data: 把時間、兵力與損失排在一起，這場戰爭的規模才算清楚。戰端自一八九九年二月四日起，到一九〇二年七月一日《華盛頓條約》簽署、七月四日官方宣布結束，前後三年零五個月。美軍在島上的兵力，起義之初約一萬人上下，一九〇〇年增至三萬人，一九〇一年再增至四萬人，全役先後有六萬餘名美軍人員在菲律賓服役。革命軍方面，馬洛斯政府一八九九年在各省的報告常稱可武裝三萬餘人，但美軍情報判斷真正能成建制作戰者遠少於此，實際成建制的作戰單位多在數千人至一萬餘之間。損失方面，美軍死亡約四千二百人，其中直接作戰死亡不足半數，其餘多死於霍亂、痢疾與瘧疾；革命軍軍人的死亡數字各來源差距極大，一般認為在數萬量級，但沒有可核對的完整名冊，難以給出確數。錢的方面，美國以二千萬美元自西班牙購得菲律賓，戰事本身又花去約一千萬美元。單場戰鬥的數字可以對照：一八九九年二月四日至五日的馬尼拉之戰，革命軍以船載砲位沿帕西格河進襲美軍哨位，美軍第一日傷亡二十餘人；一八九九年十二月二日的提拉德隘口之戰，革命軍以約一千至一千五百人對美軍第卅三義勇步兵團約三百五十人，美軍官方記錄為陣亡四人、受傷二十二人，守軍未能阻止美軍通過隘口；同一支革命軍在對西班牙作戰的最後一役——一八九九年九月至十二月的巴萊爾圍城——以六十名守軍擋住西班牙軍四個多月，戰後僅十餘人仍能作戰。距離與射擊數據同樣具體：三吋線膛野戰砲最大射程約五千八百公尺，葛拉格－約根森步槍的有效射程約四百至五百公尺，馬尼拉以北的馬洛斯距首都約五十至六十公里，位於伊羅戈省山區的提拉德隘口距馬尼拉約二百五十公里。
dataEn: Set out in time, men and losses, the scale of this war becomes clear. The shooting started on 4 February 1899 and the war was officially over on 4 July 1902, with the Treaty of Washington signed on 1 July, a span of three years and five months. American strength in the islands was about ten thousand men when the fighting began, rose to thirty thousand during 1900 and to forty thousand during 1901, and over the whole campaign more than sixty thousand American servicemen served in the Philippines. On the revolutionary side the Malolos government reported in 1899 that more than thirty thousand men were armed across the provinces, but American intelligence judged the number capable of fighting in formed units to be far lower, and the fighting formations actually observed numbered from a few thousand to somewhere over ten thousand. On losses, about four thousand two hundred Americans died, fewer than half of them in direct combat, the remainder mainly of cholera, dysentery and malaria; the figures for dead revolutionary soldiers vary enormously between sources and are generally put in the tens of thousands, but no complete roll exists to check them, so no exact number can be given. On money, the United States bought the Philippines from Spain for twenty million dollars and the war itself cost about ten million more. The figures for individual engagements can be compared: in the battle of Manila on 4 and 5 February 1899 the revolutionaries advanced along the Pasig with a boat-borne battery against American pickets, and the Americans took over twenty casualties on the first day; at the battle of Tirad Pass on 2 December 1899 a force of roughly one thousand to one thousand five hundred revolutionaries held the pass against about three hundred and fifty men of the Thirty-Third US Volunteer Infantry, the American record showing four dead and twenty-two wounded, and the defenders failed to stop the column passing through; in the last battle of the same force against Spain — the siege of Baler from September to December 1899 — sixty men held off a Spanish force for more than four months and left the field with barely a dozen still fit for duty. The figures for range and distance are just as concrete: the 3-inch field gun had a maximum range of some five thousand eight hundred metres, the effective range of the Krag-Jørgensen rifle was about four hundred to five hundred metres, Malolos lay fifty to sixty kilometres north of the capital, and Tirad Pass in the mountains of Ilocos Sur stood about two hundred and fifty kilometres from Manila.
cause: 打起來不是偶然，背景有兩層。第一層是美西戰爭的結果：一八九八年美西議和，《巴黎條約》規定西班牙將菲律賓連同波多黎各與關島割讓給美國，代價二千萬美元；美國國內對此並無共識，反對帝國主義者在國會裡佔了相當比例，參議院直到一八九九年二月六日才以五十四票對四十二票批准條約。革命軍利用了這個空檔：一八九八年五月，革命方在比亞克納巴托與西班牙總督普里莫·德·里維拉訂立的協議上分裂，接受條約的一派與拒絕條約的一派針鋒相對；五月一日馬尼拉海戰之後西班牙喪失海上補給，七八月間新任總督迪埃戈·德洛斯里奧斯又與革命方的佩德羅·帕特諾另行達成協議，革命政府一度同意解散重組。阿吉納爾多最終不願把革命的成果交回西班牙，於九月率軍入城接管，年底成立中央政府，一八九九年一月召開馬洛斯國會、通過共和憲章，宣稱菲律賓脫離西班牙而獨立，並不承認美國的主權。美國這邊則認定革命軍只是換了主人的西班牙舊部，談判屢屢破裂：一八九九年初，美方由夏夫曼委員會派出的代表在香港與阿吉納爾多接觸，要求革命方解散中央政府，改以西班牙總督身分重新接受委派，革命方認為這等於交出革命的成果而拒絕。第二層是直接導火線：一八九九年初，美軍要求革命軍退出劃定界線內的幾處據點，革命軍遲遲不動；二月四日深夜，革命軍以小股部隊沿帕西格河推進，襲擊馬尼拉北郊聖胡安德爾蒙特橋附近的美軍哨位，戰事就此爆發，雙方對起因各執一詞。還有一層容易被忽略的考量：美國必須履行對西班牙的承諾，維持馬尼拉港與亞洲航線的秩序，而革命軍的游擊與外國援助的傳聞，使華盛頓相信只有在殖民地上維持有效控制，才能保住這份投入。合法性與實力都站在革命軍一邊的美國，最後選擇用軍力解決爭議。
causeEn: The war did not spring from nothing; behind it lay two layers. The first was the result of the Spanish-American War: in 1898 the two powers made peace, and the Treaty of Paris provided that Spain should cede the Philippines, with Puerto Rico and Guam, to the United States for twenty million dollars. There was no settled consensus in the country over that acquisition, and anti-imperialists formed a substantial body in Congress, the Senate ratifying the treaty only on 6 February 1899 by fifty-four votes to forty-two. The revolutionaries made use of the gap: in May 1898 they split over the pact concluded at Biak-na-Bato with the Spanish governor-general Fernando Primo de Rivera, one party accepting it and another refusing it; after the battle of Manila Bay on 1 May left Spain without sea supply, the new governor-general Diego de los Ríos reached a separate agreement in the summer with Pedro Paterno of the revolutionary side, and the revolutionary government for a time agreed to disband and reconstitute itself. Aguinaldo in the end would not hand the fruits of the revolution back to Spain, marched into the city and took it over in September, and before the year ended set up a central government; in January 1899 the Congress at Malolos was convened and the republican charter passed, declaring the Philippines independent of Spain and refusing to acknowledge American sovereignty. The American side, for its part, regarded the revolutionaries as the old Spanish administration with new masters, and the negotiations broke down repeatedly: in the early months of 1899 representatives sent by the Schurman Commission met Aguinaldo in Hong Kong and asked the revolutionary side to disband the central government and accept appointment again as Spanish governor-general, which the revolutionaries read as a demand to hand back the revolution and rejected. The second layer was the immediate trigger: in the opening weeks of 1899 the Americans required the insurgents to withdraw from several positions inside a demarcation line, and the insurgents did not move; in the small hours of 4 February a small revolutionary force pushed down the Pasig and attacked an American picket near the bridge at San Juan del Monte, and the war began, each side blaming the other. A further consideration is easily overlooked: the United States was bound by its commitments to Spain to keep the port of Manila and the Asian sea lane in order, and the raids of the insurgents together with rumours of foreign aid persuaded Washington that only effective control on the ground would protect that investment. The United States, holding neither the better legal case nor the stronger force, chose in the end to settle the dispute by arms.
impact: 這場戰爭改變了菲律賓，也改變了美國的軍隊。戰端在官方名義上只打了三個月，但美軍要到一九〇二年才真正坐下來談判，這段落差本身就是最大的影響。對菲律賓而言，馬洛斯共和國的中央政府、軍隊與國會制度在三年內建立又瓦解，革命方原有的成建制部隊損失殆盡，剩餘武力以小股游擊隊的形式在邦板牙、卡迪巴沼澤與三描治海岸一帶延續抵抗。美軍解散革命政府的同時，一九〇一年成立由美方主導的菲律賓常備警察，一九〇二年再以大赦與既往不咎換取武裝團體放下武器，島內的權力關係從此改由美方重新界定。對美國而言，戰爭在國內引發反對兼併菲律賓的運動，馬克·吐溫等一批知識分子公開撰文反對，帝國主義與反帝國主義成為一九〇〇年總統選舉的爭議之一。軍事的教訓更被制度化：一八九九年以來分散的遠征軍無法用歐洲式的會戰解決殖民地問題，美軍於一九〇一年成立審查委員會調查薩馬爾的戰事，同時推動參謀部制度的改革，一九〇四年成立參謀總部，並在師級部隊內實驗更靈活的機動作戰編制，這套想法後來成為第一次世界大戰前美國陸軍現代化的方向。經濟上，麻、椰、煙等菲出口作物大量進入美國市場，美國商船隊把群島接入了環太平洋航線，港口與鐵路的營運也逐步由美資接手；與此同時，遠征的經驗也暴露了美國海軍在亞洲的遠洋補給與煤水補給問題，後來成為海軍擴軍計劃的重要理由。
impactEn: The war changed the Philippines, and it changed the American army as well. Officially the shooting lasted only three months, but the Americans did not sit down to negotiate until 1902, and that gap is itself the largest single effect. For the Philippines, the central government, the army and the parliamentary institutions of the Malolos Republic were built and then dismantled within three years; the revolutionary formations were worn out, and the residue of military power continued as small guerrilla bands through the Pampanga, the Candaba marshes and the Zambales coast. Alongside the dissolution of the revolutionary government the Americans created a constabulary under their own control in 1901, and in 1902 used amnesty and forgiveness in exchange for armed groups to lay down their weapons, so that the balance of power on the islands was redrawn under American direction. In the United States the war produced a movement against the annexation of the Philippines; Mark Twain and a number of other writers argued the case openly, and imperialism and anti-imperialism became one of the issues contested in the presidential election of 1900. The military lesson was put into institutional form: a dispersed expeditionary army, it had been shown, could not settle a colonial question by European-style pitched battle, so a board of inquiry was convened in 1901 to examine the Samar campaign, reform of the General Staff was pushed forward, the General Staff was established in 1904, and a more flexible maneuver formation was experimented with at division level, an idea that would run through the modernisation of the US Army before the First World War. Economically, Philippine exports of hemp, copra and tobacco entered the American market in volume, American merchant shipping tied the islands into the trans-Pacific routes, and the operation of the ports and railways passed progressively into American hands. At the same time the experience of the expedition laid bare the problems of long-distance supply and coaling for the American navy in Asian waters, which later became a principal argument for naval expansion.
result: 一九〇二年三月二十八日，阿吉納爾多在伊羅戈省北部的藏身處被美軍搜索分隊發現；隨行的將領已相繼離他而去，他同意隨軍前往，之後被押往碧瑤。七月一日《華盛頓條約》在華盛頓簽訂，一方是美國，一方是西班牙，條約中西班牙以一百萬美元的清償金額放棄對菲律賓的一切權利聲索；同日，美國與革命方代表在馬尼拉另立文件，馬洛斯共和國的殘餘政府接受美國的宗主權，隨後被解散。七月四日，戰事以官方公告告終。就軍事而言，美軍完成了三件難事：佔據了從馬尼拉到卡迪巴的交通線，把革命方逐出主要城鎮，並在大規模遠征結束後仍靠小分隊與地方部隊維持鄉村控制。革命軍一方則失去中央政府的運作能力與成建制部隊，倖存的指揮官在護都計畫下分散成游擊隊，最後一批武裝在巴萊爾、卡迪巴與三描治一帶於一九〇二年至一九〇三年間陸續放下武器，摩洛的戰事則延續到更晚。兵器層面的結果可以這樣看：卡面這類前裝線膛野戰砲在這場戰爭裡完成了最後一次實戰，美軍在一九〇四年以新造的後膛野戰砲取代三吋線膛野戰砲成為標準配備，革命軍手中的舊銅砲多數被拆毀或散失，只餘少量作為戰史陳列留在原處。一場戰爭結束了，但另一場更長的戰爭——美國對菲律賓的統治——才剛剛開始。
resultEn: On 28 March 1902 Aguinaldo was found by an American search detachment in his hiding place in northern Ilocos Norte; his generals had already left him one after another, and he agreed to go with the troops and was afterwards taken to Baguio. The Treaty of Washington was signed at Washington on 1 July, between the United States and Spain, Spain renouncing all claim to the Philippines in return for the settlement of one million dollars; on the same day a separate instrument was signed at Manila between the Americans and representatives of the revolution, the remnant government of the Malolos Republic accepting American sovereignty and being dissolved soon after. On 4 July the war was ended by official announcement. Militarily the Americans achieved three difficult things: they held the line of communication from Manila to Candaba, they drove the revolutionaries out of the principal towns, and after the great expeditions had ended they still maintained control of the countryside with detachments and local forces. On the revolutionary side the central government lost its capacity to function and its formed units were gone; the surviving commanders dispersed into guerrilla bands under a plan to defend the capital, and the last armed groups in the regions of Baler, Candaba and Zambales laid down their weapons between 1902 and 1903, while the fighting in the Moro country continued for years longer. The result at the level of weapons can be put this way: the muzzle-loading field gun of the kind shown on this card fought its last war here, the American Army replaced the 3-inch muzzle-loading field gun with the new breech-loading field gun of 1902 as its standard equipment in 1904, and most of the old brass guns in revolutionary hands were broken up or lost, only a few remaining on the spot as relics of the war. One war had ended, but another and much longer one — the American government of the Philippines — had only just begun.
